pairs.evidence: scripts/case-loops/effort/triage.ts:112 The resume filter counts any unit marked 'triaged' as done. triage.ts:450 sets that stage when the unit is picked for the army, not when its result comes back. So an MP whose subagent never returned a proposal is left out of every later army and is still counted as 'dossiered' coverage.

techniques.evidence: scripts/case-loops/effort/triage.ts:112 ledger.json is the durable roster, but resume trusts its 'triaged' claim without checking it against the harvested payloads. finalize-ledger.ts:6 says the opposite ('a unit left at "triaged" would be re-dispatched'), so the two writers of one record disagree about what the record means.

scripts/case-loops/effort/finalize-ledger.ts:23 The unit stage is an open string retyped in each script (triage.ts has its own PriorUnit type), not a closed, single-sourced vocabulary. 'triaged' means both 'admitted to the army' and 'processed, awaiting persist' (finalize-ledger.ts:61).

scripts/case-loops/effort/merge-batch.ts:40 Roster accounting exists but only warns. The merged payload is still written, and its note claims it was 'cross-checked' against the full army. There is no claimed-without-result, failed or lost class, so accounts need not sum to the roster. Duplicates are silently kept first (line 28).

scripts/case-loops/effort/gate.ts:216 The parent checks decidable leaves in code against the graph (id membership, forbidden props, namespacing, closed vocabulary, verdict rung) and exits 2 on drops. Undecidable prose checks are only warnings and never promote a verdict.

scripts/case-loops/effort/merge-batch.ts:66 A verdict that arrives with no review state gets the bottom 'machine' rung, never a promoted one. An existing decided state is passed through unchanged (lines 62-64).
scripts/case-loops/effort/extract-dossiers.ts:2 Executors get a pre-extracted input file and never hold a database connection. Writes go back through the orchestrator's merge, gate and persist path.

pairs.registryProposal: result-harvest could name a common file-based-ledger failure: the dispatch-time stage ('admitted') is reused as the resume filter's 'done' predicate, so a missing result turns into permanent false coverage rather than a re-dispatch.
